newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait stocks hit record high after debt payment.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait stocks hit record high after debt payment.

text.p: Kuwait's share index hit its fourth record high so far in September on Sunday with record volume and value levels amid relief that a bad debt payment deadline passed without stock sell-offs, dealers said.
"Confidence in the market is increasing. The bad debts (payment) did not cause any share dumping and capital is flowing to the market," said a dealer.
Most debtors owing billions of dinars (dollars) met a September 6 deadline to pay millions of dinars in a plan to settle chronic bad debt with an original value of $20 billion, bankers said.
The debt is owed to the state by some 10,000 debtors.
The index finished at 1,659.4 points, a rise of 11.4 points, or 0.69 percent compared to Saturday's 1,648 points record high.
Officials said volume amounted to 265.4 million shares and value reached 48.4 million dinars ($161.8 million), also hitting new all-time highs. They did not provide comparative figures.
Dealers said the end of the summer holidays was another reason for the increased activity, adding that talk of privatisation plans had also boosted the market.
After the 1991 Gulf War the government announced plans to shed its stake in about 60 local firms and, at a later stage, state-run services such as electricity and water.
"The market is strong. Just look at the results," Mohammad Jassem, a private dealer said.
Many listed firms reported healthy mid-year results, indicating prospects of large dividend payments at the end of the year.
